1	# Entire for Orca: plan
2	
3	Bring Entire (trails, findings, approvals, checkpoints) into Orca's UI as an Orca plugin, the way
4	Orca already surfaces GitHub pull requests and checks.
5	
6	Status: phases 0 and 0.5 done, and a stopgap Entire panel works from a development folder. Next:
7	phase 1 spikes.
8	
9	## Environment
10	
11	- Orca desktop runs on Windows (1.4.245). Plugins are in alpha: manifest format 2, host API 1.0.
12	- Most Orca and Entire projects live in WSL (`\\wsl.localhost\Ubuntu\...`). Others live
13	  on a VPS that Orca reaches as a paired Orca server (`orca environment list`: "Endo VPS Server", an
14	  orcad over an SSH tunnel to `ubuntu@15.204.88.195`).
15	- Entire CLI `0.12.3-nightly` on both sides: WSL (keyring login) and Windows in `%USERPROFILE%\.local\bin`
16	  (Credential Manager login).
17	- This repo: `C:\Users\pcruc\Web Projects\orca-entire-extension`, origin
18	  `entire://aws-us-east-2.entire.io/et/entire-repos/orca-entire-extension`, Entire enabled.
19	
20	## What Orca's plugin API allows today (1.4.245)
21	
22	Sources: `docs/reference/plugin-*.md` and `src/shared/plugins/**` in github.com/stablyai/orca.
23	
24	- `execution: "trusted-worker"`: `main` runs in a Node process Orca forks on the desktop host (Windows
25	  here). It has full Node access, but its env is an allowlist (PATH, HOME, USERPROFILE, TEMP and a few
26	  Windows system variables; no APPDATA). Idle workers stop after 5 minutes with nothing in flight, and a
27	  command must answer within 30 seconds.
28	- Host API 1.0: `workspace.readContext` returns `{ branch, displayName, terminals: [{ id }] }` with no
29	  path; `notifications.show`; `terminal.sendText` (worker only); `storage.*`, `secrets.*` and
30	  `settings.*` (worker only).
31	- Events (at most 3): `workspace.created`, `workspace.removed`, `agent.status.changed`.
32	- The command palette ignores a command's return value. The Run button in Settings → Plugins shows its
33	  first 200 characters in a toast. Worker stdout and stderr go to the plugin's Logs (last 200 lines).
34	- Panels are sealed: Orca injects CSP `connect-src 'none'` (scripts and styles inline only, images
35	  as data URLs), blocks links and `window.open`, and gives a panel no channel to its own worker. A
36	  panel can call only `workspace.readContext` and `notifications.show`, and loads one HTML file.
37	- Stopgap: Orca rereads a development folder's panel file whenever the folder changes and remounts
38	  the panel when the HTML differs. Writing a file there neither restarts the worker nor asks for
39	  approval again (only shortcuts and VM recipes tie approval to file bytes). So the worker writes its
40	  data into the panel file. Installed copies are hash-checked and refused once a byte changes, so
41	  this works only from a development folder.
42	- Stopgap for the panel's ↻: a panel's only mutation is `notifications.show`, which Orca records in
43	  `plugins-data\audit.log` as `titleChars=<n>`. The button shows a notification with a title length
44	  no worker notice uses, and a running worker watches the log. Orca's 5-minute idle timer resets on
45	  the worker's own host calls, so once started the worker calls `readContext` every 5 seconds and
46	  stays up with Orca. A keyboard shortcut is no way out: in
47	  a development folder, keybindings tie approval to every file, so each panel write would need a new
48	  review.
49	- Reserved but not shipped: `taskSources`, `statusBarItems`, `sidebarCards`, `connections`, `settings`,
50	  `hooks`, `skills`, `mcpServers`.
51	- The installed build has no `orca plugin ...` CLI (it is on Orca's `main`). Load the plugin through
52	  Settings → Plugins → Development folders.
53	- On 1.4.245 the manifest must keep `publisher` (leaving it out needs `>=1.4.246`). When distributing,
54	  it must equal the GitHub owner of the repository Orca installs from. Ids may not start with `orca-`.
55

content.text:
Each finding card now has its own copy icon, and the Findings heading has one that copies them all.

**What I changed** (`panel/template.html`)
- **One finding:** the copy icon sits at the top-right of the card, next to the confidence. Clicking it copies that finding without opening or closing the card.
- **All findings:** the icon in the Findings heading copies every finding in the list. That includes resolved and dismissed ones, since they're listed too. Findings are separated by `---`.
- **What gets copied:** plain text you can paste into an agent prompt or an issue:
  ```
  [HIGH] Null deref
  src/a.mjs:4–9
  Status: Dismissed        (only when it isn't open, or is stale)

  <the finding's full text>

  Dismissed: <the reason>
  ```
- **Feedback:** after a click the icon turns into a green check for 1.5 seconds, or a red ✕ if the copy failed.

**How the copy works:** Orca's panel frames get no browser permissions, so `navigator.clipboard` is refused. Orca's own frame policy (`plugin-frame-session-policies.ts`) says `execCommand('copy')` still works during a click. The buttons use that, through a hidden textarea.

I added a test in `test/panel.test.mjs` that checks the copied text using the panel's own functions. All 69 tests pass, and the panel's script still parses. I haven't clicked the buttons in Orca, so I haven't seen a real copy succeed yet. The worker code didn't change, so pressing ↻ in the panel should be enough to pick up the new template.
